LESSON: WEATHER AND THE SKY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: NATURAL ENVIRONMENT Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learn
Topic 2.1: Weather and the Sky
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Weather and the Sky, part of NATURAL ENVIRONMENT Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learn in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How is the weather today? 2. How does the sky look like at night and during the day?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Weather and the Sky together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: Interacting with technology as learners design and create audio recordings for stories about weather or a

day with specific weather event

• Creativity and imagination: Originality skills as learners tell stories about weather or a day with specific weather events.

Values:
Responsibility: Resilience is enhanced as learners engage in making and maintaining a daily journal on weather conditions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Life skills Issues: Self-esteem as learners observe and share ideas on prevailing weather conditions.

• Social-Economic Issues: Environmental education as learners predict the weather conditions.

29

Link to other Learning Areas:

Religious Education Activities: Creation of the Sky as learners share ideas on prevailing weather conditions as an outdoor

activity and make a weather chart.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Approved learning support materials, Sky (immediate environment with suitable environmental adaptations), theme based

Pictures/Photographs/Flash cards/ charts with legible print and appropriate colour contrast on weather and the sky, heavy gauge

Manilla papers, Adapted Pencils, marker pens and crayons with enhanced grip, hand stabilizers, pencil grips, adapted digital

devices (computers/ video players/ speakers/ audio-visual recorders/ smart phones) with appropriate accessibility features and

software, foot-boards, slates,

Core Competencies to be Developed:

• Communication and collaboration: Listening and speaking skills as learners recite/ mime poems and sing/ hum songs on

playing with soil.

• Citizenship: Information and communication skills as learners model different objects using soil together.

Values:

• Unity: Co-operation is nurtured as learners take roles while modelling different objects using soil.

• Social justice: Co-operation is enhanced as learners take turns to fill and empty cans with soil for fun.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCI
s) :

• Health Promotion Issues: Prevention of illnesses as learners clean up/tidy up the working space and own hands after

modelling in purposive groups.

• Life skills: Interpersonal relationships as learners use common courteous words as they observe game rules when playing

with soil.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Mathematics Activities: Measurement of mass as learners play with soil such as filling empty cans.
